objective: Identify the working PR branch and exact built Pi extension source and install destination for the user-requested installation.
scope: Read-only investigation of the local checkout, PRs #125 and #130 through gh, and relevant Pi installation/configuration files.
Do not modify files, install anything, switch branches, or write version-control state.
constraints: Use gh to inspect PR branches and their file contents, because the user explicitly requested it.
Run any delegated Pi process with provider kimi-coding and model kimi-for-coding, the registered provider ID for the requested model.
Establish what packages/integrations/pi/dist/extensions/.pi/ contains and whether it is the built extension to install, the destination, or an unrelated artifact.
Determine the exact install command or copy destination from repository documentation and Pi configuration; do not guess.
Keep working until the source, destination and verification command are established; stop only if a required fact cannot be obtained.
Report in under 300 words with exact paths and commands.

criteria.text: PR selection: identify whether PR #125, PR #130, or another PR supplies the working built Pi extension, citing gh evidence and check status.

result:
## Report — assignment-0mwkngvo1-v2rh

**PR selection.** PR #130 (`release/0.3.4/feat/final-guidance-events`, "feat: complete 0.3.4 with shared Core and native tools") supplies the working built Pi extension: `gh` file API shows its head carries `packages/integrations/pi/dist/extensions/holyagent.js` at sha `6ecaf41` (1,247,944 bytes), while the identical `fd809ba` (781,681 bytes) sits on `main`, `dev` and PR #125's head — PR #125's diff never touches the bundle, it only changes `dist/scripts` and `dist/package.json`. Check status: PR #125 is fully green; PR #130 passes `check`, `installers`, `branch-model` but its `macos`/`windows` jobs are CANCELLED (an earlier run shows a `validation / macos` FAILURE) — so #130 is the extension source, with platform checks not green.

**Install paths.** Built extension source: `packages/integrations/pi/dist/extensions/holyagent.js` on branch `release/0.3.4/feat/final-guidance-events` (package root `packages/integrations/pi/dist`, `pi` key → `./extensions`; docs/pi/extensions.md §The HolyAgent package). Documented install (docs/pi/installation.md): global `pi install git:github.com/davidbasilefilho/holyagent@release/0.3.4/feat/final-guidance-events`, or local build `pi install <worktree>/packages/integrations/pi/dist` (local folder used as-is). Declaration lands in `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` `packages` (currently `[]`); git/npm sources land in `~/.pi/agent/npm/`; `-l` instead writes the project's `.pi/settings.json`. The untracked `packages/integrations/pi/dist/extensions/.pi/settings.json` (`{"packages": ["..\holyagent.js"]}`) is a stray experiment: unreferenced by any repo source, not a Pi discovery path (`~/.pi/agent/extensions/` or `.pi/extensions/`), and it names a bare `.js` instead of a package root, so it is neither the built extension nor a working install.

**Verification (non-destructive).** `pi list` (proves the package configured/installable; non-zero exit on package failure), then a headless load proof: `pi -ne -e <dist>\extensions\holyagent.js --print --provider kimi-coding --model kimi-for-coding "reply: loaded"` — loads only this extension, one turn, no state writes. `holyagent doctor` additionally verifies the package is listed in Pi's settings.

No files modified; nothing installed; branch untouched.
